answer: Mechanism: an eSIM-bound identity bond. Each applicant buys a carrier-verified eSIM, posts a 20 USDC deposit, and passes a live face-to-NFC-passport check that anchors the SIM to a real document; the passport number hashes to a registry so one passport maps to one account. A duplicate attempt is proven within an hour and slashes the deposit, which the honest reporter receives. An attacker needs 300 real eSIMs at $4, 300 KYC passes at $25 each, and 6,000 USDC escrowed: $13,200 and two weeks. At the nadir of a sybil wave the tide turns, and accounts that wander onto that shore get burned.
